cadence: Weekly news picks, refreshed every Monday alongside citation rankings.
selection: The top stories from the trailing 30 days, scored on publisher authority, discussion volume, whether a concrete verifiable result is reported, whether it changes what agent builders do now, whether an artifact was released, and expected durability. Only primary sources are cited, and performance claims remain attributed to their publishers.

items.title: The components of agent memory
items.why: Anthropic separates transcripts, memory notes, wikis and injected context, and tests offline dreaming to correct and reorganize them. On 25 internal-document questions it reports 61% of graded criteria with search plus a grown wiki, versus 53% with search alone.

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.why: The authors use latent-space agent swarms and KV-cache exchange for evolutionary program search. On 21 mathematical and scientific-computing problems, they report matching competing frameworks’ 60-minute best scores in a median 3–8 minutes.

items.source: Genoria AI Team et al. · arXiv
items.title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design
items.why: The authors evolve both harness assets and enzyme-design algorithms. They report 10 of 32 non-pre-specified luciferase candidates with at least twice wild-type activity, plus prospective A3A and polymerase tests; physical-loop results are distinguished from development-set optimization.

items.title: SelfImprove-Bench: Evaluating Generalization in Self-Improving Agents
items.why: The authors introduce a reproducible RSI benchmark with a G0–G4 generalization ladder spanning exploration, planning and reasoning, and report that evolution gains do not consistently transfer across levels.

items.title: Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime
items.why: The authors let an agent revise its harness during ongoing work behind a protected activation layer. Against a fixed-policy control, they report 35–61% lower held-out model cost on AppWorld and SREGym with comparable correctness.

items.title: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight
items.why: Mistral releases the improved 1T-parameter multimodal flagship weights under its Ecosystem Open-Weight license. It reports 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 48% on the Coding Agent Index, with 47% fewer tokens than GLM-5.3 on the latter.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
items.why: Google announces Carbon for long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity, reporting 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro. Access begins with pre-release testing and selected cyber defenders through Fairwind; general developer and consumer access is still forthcoming.

items.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
items.why: OpenAI releases a model for visual reasoning and computer use in Work, Codex and the API. It reports a 15-point Agents’ Last Exam gain over GPT-5.6 Terra at medium effort at about one-third the cost, and 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at max effort.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro series is live
items.why: Moonshot’s 3T-class multimodal flagship has a 1M-token context window and is available in Kimi products and the API. Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0; the official Hugging Face repository now contains downloadable weights.

items.title: Introducing Flint
items.why: Recursive releases a 40B-total / 2.5B-active MoE for local agentic coding and says its Eureka Machine helped develop the architecture, data, training, quantization and inference stack. The official post reports over 125 tokens/s on an M4 Pro at short contexts.
